_readme: Rows are use-site requests, columns are @font-face font-style descriptors. Addresses (A1, B2, ...) are labels fixed on 2026-09-20, in the order an author would write the @font-face rules (renumbered twice the same day: italic fonts were dropped, then the font-variation-settings row, which tests precedence, not matching). File names use the slugs: matrix-{row}-{column}.html. `request` is the element's font-style as the reference sees it; the generator derives the test's inline CSS from it (or from `fvs` / `extraCss`).

font.note: real Cairo subset (slnt -11..11, wght 200..1000, no ital); the test glyph is the capital I

columns.name: The font's own range
columns.note: Declared oblique with the font's true slnt range

columns.name: Past the break-point
columns.note: Declared oblique past CSS's 14deg break-point: the smallest range that reaches beyond the font's own limit (11) and still contains every angle CSS can imply (14deg for bare oblique, 11deg for italic). Ranges are inclusive, so rows 2, 3 and 6 probe the boundary exactly.

columns.name: Narrow, one-sided range
columns.note: Declared oblique, inside the font's range and excluding the negative side (the pattern of Inter's slnt -10..0)

columns.name: Auto
columns.note: Descriptor omitted = auto, the initial value. Selected as if normal, but not clamped, so the font's own slnt range applies

standalone.name: font-style: auto renders exactly like an omitted descriptor
normal against a backslant-only face (oblique -20deg -5deg) falls back to slnt 5
